title: Redwood POC scoping with Lakeshore Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security & compliance requirements for a 4-week pilot. Confirmed success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and security controls needed: SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO (SAML) + IdP integration, RBAC scoping, immutable audit logs, encryption/KMS, and network isolation (VPC). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 kit and SAML integration doc, Lakeshore to provide sample workload, and schedule benchmark run week 2.
next_steps: Redwood: Send SOC 2 / ISO evidence and security questionnaire by 2027-10-03
Customer: Provide representative sample dataset and expected qps by 2027-10-05
Redwood SE: Share SAML IdP integration guide and test tenant details by 2027-10-04
Schedule benchmark run (week of 2027-10-11) and finalize success criteria before run
action_items: Jordan Lee: send pricing + SOC2 kit - due 2027-10-03
Priya Nair: prepare benchmark plan and test tenant - due 2027-10-08

transcript:
Header: 2027-09-30 14:00 PT | Duration: 62 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Emily (Lakeshore), Tom (Lakeshore), Aisha (Lakeshore), Ben (Lakeshore)

Summary (auto): POC scoping for a security-first pilot. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and required security/compliance artifacts (SOC 2 / ISO, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS).

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros, then we'll run through the pilot goals and especially the security checklist Tom asked for.
00:12 Emily: Thanks Jordan. Emily here, head of clinical AI. We're evaluating Redwood for an inference layer to power our summarization and triage workflows. Security is non-negotiable for this pilot.
00:20 Tom: Hi, Tom, Security Architect. I'll be driving the compliance gating. We need SOC 2 evidence, ISO 27001 if available, and details on SSO/SAML and audit logs.
00:30 Jordan: Totally. Priya will run the tech details. Priya, quick overview?
00:34 Priya: Sure. Thanks. So the typical pilot we run is 3-4 weeks. Week 1: onboarding + sample data ingest, week 2: benchmark runs, week 3: tuning and validation, week 4: wrap-up and decision. For security we can run in hosted isolated tenancy or a private VPC deployment depending on your needs.
00:55 Marcus: we'll also provide a test tenant with RBAC and a SAML flow if you want to try SSO later in the pilot.
01:05 Aisha: On the infra side, we want to know network isolation options. Can Redwood spin up a VPC peering or private deployment? We prefer not to send PHI over public endpoints.
01:16 Priya: Yes. For pilots we support private VPC peering and, for stricter setups, a private deployment package. For the pilot we can do a VPC peering + customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your control.
01:30 Tom: Good. SOC 2: do you have a current report? And do you have ISO 27001? We'll need the auditor details for validation.
01:38 Jordan: We do have a SOC 2 Type II report; I'll share the certified report and an executive summary. We're collecting ISO evidence too - we have some ISO-aligned controls but not a full certification in all regions; I'll clarify in the packet.
01:52 Emily: What's in the SOC 2 kit? Does it include pen test details and encryption-at-rest specifics?
01:59 Jordan: The kit includes the SOC 2 report, policy summaries, encryption at rest/in transit descriptions, KMS integration notes, and an audit contact. Pen test reports sometimes are redacted but we include the summary.
02:12 Ben: From product, success criteria: latency under 300ms 95th percentile for 512-token gen, throughput to support 50 concurrent clinical triage users (estimated 20 rps), and semantic quality measured by accuracy on our 100-case eval set - target > 85% F1. Also no PII leakage.
02:33 Priya: Ok, concrete metric. For latency we can benchmark using your average sequence lengths; if 512 tokens 95p under 300ms that's aggressive on shared hosted but achievable on Dedicated or private with quantization. We'll size GPUs accordingly.
02:48 Aisha: Our expected workload for the pilot: steady-state 20 qps, bursts to 60 qps for short windows; avg request 450 tokens, peak 1200 tokens. Daily token volume around 5 million.
03:05 Priya: That's helpful. For 20 qps steady at 450 tokens, we recommend starting with a small dedicated pool for predictable latency. We can also test autoscaling policies. We'll draft a recommended config.
03:18 Tom: Audit logs: we need immutable logs of request metadata, user identity, timestamps, and model/version used. Retention for the pilot: 90 days minimum, exportable to your SIEM (Splunk/Elastic). Do you support signed immutable logs?
03:34 Marcus: We stream structured audit events with request id, user id, route, model version, and token counts. For pilots we can enable a write-once export to your S3 with server-side encryption and manifesting; signing depends on your compliance team but we can provide HMAC-signed log manifests.
03:51 Tom: We also need RBAC to enforce least privilege - dev access vs audit-only. Can you map to our directory groups?
03:58 Priya: Yes, we support SAML-based SSO and can map IdP groups to roles (admin, developer, auditor). Policies can restrict who can create model rollouts or view raw request payloads.
04:12 Aisha: KMS - can we bring our own key or use HSM-backed keys? We can't have keys in Redwood-managed KMS for this pilot.
04:20 Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and dedicated setups; for hosted tenants there's an option to bring keys via an HSM integration in certain regions. For the pilot, VPC + BYOK is doable.
04:33 Ben: About data residency: all processing must be within the US region. Is that configurable for the test tenant?
04:40 Marcus: Yes, we'll pin the deployment to the US-east region. For private deployments we can run on-prem if needed but that takes more time.
04:48 Emily: Ok timeline wise, what's realistic? We need the pilot to finish within 4 weeks so internal stakeholders can decide by mid-November.
04:55 Priya: Proposed timeline: kickoff and onboarding (week 0), benchmark and load testing (week 1-2), tuning and remediation (week 3), final review and decision (week 4). So four weeks total.
05:08 Jordan: We'll need your sample dataset and expected qps by next Tuesday to meet that timeline.
05:14 Aisha: We'll provide sample de-identified transcripts and an expected traffic profile by Monday EOD.
05:21 Tom: A few more clarifications: do you provide SOC 2 scoping questions as a spreadsheet for our procurement team?
05:28 Jordan: Yes, we'll include the security questionnaire responses and the SOC 2 report. We'll also include our technical contact for the auditor.
05:35 Ben: On benchmarks, we want to run both latency/throughput and quality evals. Can Redwood run an automated benchmark harness?
05:43 Priya: Absolutely. We'll run the harness against your test tenant. Benchmarks we propose: synthetic load (qps sweep), concurrency tests, and an eval script that scores your 100-case set. We'll surface token-level cost, tail latency distribution, and model output diffs.
05:58 Emily: Do you support KV cache or prefix caching that might affect latencies? There's mention of KV cash in some docs I saw - is that the same as KV cache?
06:06 Marcus: yes, KV cache (cache) - apologies for the docs typo - we support prefix caching and per-customer KV cache to reduce repeated prefix costs; we'll document expected gains. For clinical triage it can reduce latency significantly for repeated prompts.
06:20 Tom: On encryption in transit and at rest: TLS + AES-256 at rest is fine, but we need details on key rotation.
06:27 Jordan: key rotation policies are documented in the SOC kit. For customer-managed keys you control rotation; for Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our policy and provide rotation history to auditors.
06:38 Aisha: What about SSO test flow? We want to validate SAML and map groups before exposing raw logs to devs.
06:46 Priya: We'll spin up a SAML test tenant. Steps: you provide IdP metadata, we configure SAML, you run a smoke SSO test, then we map groups to roles. We can make an auditor-only role that strips payloads.
06:58 Tom: Great. Anything about model provenance? We need immutable record of model version and weights used for each inference in audits.
07:06 Marcus: Every request includes model id and version in the audit event. We can also snapshot the model config used for the run and store a manifest with the logs.
07:16 Emily: On quality success criteria: we want >85% F1 on our 100-case eval and no critical regressions vs your baseline. If quality drops, pilot fails.
07:28 Priya: We'll run the evaluation harness and share the baseline. If the model doesn't meet the threshold, we'll explore prompt engineering, quantization tradeoffs, or a different model variant. We'll include a rollback plan.
07:43 Ben: Cost controls during pilot - we need token limits and alerting if costs exceed thresholds.
07:49 Jordan: We can set quotas and alerts per project, and cap usage to avoid bill surprises.
07:56 Tom: Legal/procurement - we'll likely need a short DPA addendum for the pilot indicating data processing specifics. Procurement will review SOC2 and the DPA.
08:05 Jordan: Understood. We'll attach our standard DPA and a pilot-specific addendum with limited retention and export controls.
08:13 Emily: Ok, can we recap the success criteria and acceptance items?
08:17 Jordan: Sure. Success criteria recap: 1) Latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for 512-token workload (or matched config on dedicated) 2) Throughput: handle steady 20 qps and short bursts to 60 qps with <5% error rate 3) Quality: >85% F1 on 100-case eval 4) Security: SOC 2 evidence provided, SAML SSO working, RBAC configured, audit logs exportable to SIEM, BYOK KMS configured 5) Data residency: processing in US region.
08:52 Tom: That looks good. For the audit logs we also want a retention test - can Redwood materialize the logs to our S3 and then we validate log integrity?
08:59 Marcus: Yes. We'll push logs to your S3 bucket with manifest and signature. You can validate integrity and retention.
09:08 Priya: Next steps: Jordan will send the SOC 2 kit and security questionnaire. Priya will provide the benchmark plan and a preconfigured test tenant. Customer provides sample data and IdP metadata. Then we schedule the benchmark the week of Oct 11.
09:24 Emily: Sounds good. A couple of notes: our compliance team sometimes wants to see penetration test summaries and tracker for open CVEs. Can you include a short SecOps summary?
09:34 Jordan: We'll include SecOps summary and CVE tracker info as part of the packet.
09:40 Aisha: Any blockers for SAML? The IdP we use is Okta.
09:44 Priya: Okta is supported and commonly used. We just need SAML metadata and an admin account to test mapping.
09:51 Ben: On the pilot: if everything passes, what's the path to Dedicated or Private? Cost and timeline?
09:57 Jordan: If pilot meets success criteria, we present options: Dedicated reserved pool (1-3 month lead time depending on region) or Private deployment for on-prem (longer lead time, procurement/licensing). We'll provide estimates in the follow-up.
10:09 Tom: One more security question - do you support customer-supplied HSM for key ops?
10:14 Marcus: For private deployments we support HSM integrations. For hosted pilots we can support customer-managed keys in supported regions; full HSM bring-your-own is typically part of an enterprise contract. We'll note this.
10:25 Jordan: Ok, we'll capture action items. Any final questions?
10:29 Emily: None from me. Thanks, everyone.
10:31 Tom: No, thanks.
10:33 Jordan: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the packet and SAML test tenant details.

Auto-generated Action Items (transcript): Jordan - share SOC2 kit, DPA; Priya - benchmark plan and test tenant; Aisha - sample data and IdP metadata; Tom - compliance contacts.

End of call.
